headline: Bulls Return From a Strong Friday, But Hormuz Uncertainty Clouds the Open
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious start Monday morning as traders carry forward Friday's broad gains while keeping one eye on the Strait of Hormuz. The prior session closed with unmistakable strength — 414 of 549 names in our universe advanced versus just 133 decliners — yet geopolitical noise over the weekend has tempered early enthusiasm. Iran signaled over the weekend that any reopening of the strategically critical waterway remains conditional on meaningful U.S. concessions across multiple demands, leaving energy markets in a holding pattern as Gulf investors were already reported subdued awaiting clarity.

Friday's session was led by Semiconductors, which surged 3.81%, followed by Homebuilders at 2.62% and Software at 2.32%. Consumer and Materials both cleared 2%, while Healthcare added 1.64%. Energy was the lone sector in the red, off 0.54%, weighed by the same Hormuz uncertainty now greeting Monday's open. Oil is described as steady but unable to rally on any swift resolution optimism.

The week ahead carries two widely flagged focal points for equity markets. Earnings-driven single-stock moves from Friday — including a 35.25% surge in Corsair Gaming and a 24.89% jump in Twilio — serve as a reminder that individual catalysts remain potent. Watch the energy complex and any Iran-related headlines at the open as the primary swing factors for early tape direction.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Standoff Keeps Oil Bulls in Check
briefs.body: Iran over the weekend linked any reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to a package of concessions from the United States, dampening near-term hopes for a resolution. Crude held broadly steady on the news rather than rallying, underscoring how much of a swift deal had already been priced out. Gulf bourses were reported subdued as regional investors awaited firmer signals.

briefs.headline: Corsair Gaming Rockets 35% on Earnings Catalyst
briefs.body: Corsair Gaming posted the sharpest single-session gain in our universe on Friday, climbing 35.25% in what appears to be a decisive earnings or guidance beat. The move catapulted the gaming-hardware specialist to the top of the leaderboard by a wide margin. Momentum traders will be watching whether the stock can hold its gains when broader volume returns Monday.

briefs.headline: Twilio Surges as Cloud Communications Demand Reasserts Itself
briefs.body: Communications-platform provider Twilio advanced 24.89% on Friday, suggesting the market received fresh evidence of accelerating demand in the cloud-software segment. The move helped lift the broader Software sector to a 2.32% gain for the session. Analysts will be parsing any forward guidance commentary for durability signals heading into the new week.

briefs.headline: Trade Desk Sinks Nearly 22%, Dragging Ad-Tech Sentiment
briefs.body: Internet advertising-technology firm Trade Desk fell 21.90% on Friday, the steepest decline in our universe and a stark outlier against an otherwise buoyant tape. The drop signals that investors received disappointing results or guidance from the digital-advertising bellwether. Given Trade Desk's role as a barometer for programmatic ad spending, the ripple effects may weigh on related names early Monday.

briefs.headline: Syria and Russia Settle Long-Running Dispute Over Mediterranean Bases
briefs.body: After roughly eighteen months of negotiations, Syria and Russia reached an agreement governing the future of the Tartous naval facility and Hmeimim air base. The deal resolves a significant strategic ambiguity in the eastern Mediterranean and could have modest implications for regional energy-transit risk perceptions. Markets will assess whether the accord alters the broader geopolitical calculus alongside the Iran situation.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Leads Friday's Broad Rally With Nearly 4% Gain
briefs.body: The Semiconductors group rose 3.81% on Friday, the strongest sector performance in our universe and a meaningful vote of confidence in the chip cycle. Semi-equipment name Onto Innovation gained 14.74% while Microchip Technology added 13.89%, amplifying the group's outperformance. The sector's momentum will be a key watch point at Monday's open given its outsized influence on overall market breadth.
